subject.title: fix: block unresolved Telegram reply targets

question: Should unresolved reply-target classification be owned by the Telegram plugin and exposed through a generic typed reply-context contract, or may the core reply runner permanently recognize Telegram placeholder text?
rationale: Repository policy favors plugin-owned transport interpretation, but choosing or extending the permanent cross-channel reply-context contract requires maintainer intent and coordination with the active structured-metadata work.

options.title: Use a generic typed contract
options.body: Classify the unresolved target in Telegram ingress and make core act only on an explicit channel-neutral reply-resolution fact.

options.title: Approve the core special-case
options.body: Keep the literal Telegram placeholder check in core and explicitly accept the resulting channel coupling and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Coordinate with the metadata PR
options.body: Pause this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90745 establishes the reply metadata contract, then rebase the guard onto that surface.

recommendation.title: Use a generic typed contract
recommendation.body: Classify the unresolved target in Telegram ingress and make core act only on an explicit channel-neutral reply-resolution fact.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work connects this person to the core auto-reply routing boundary where the permanent ownership decision must land.
